, be grateful for all the good things your body
does for you. It rides bikes, lifts weights at the gym, goes canoeing, and lets
you have fun. How could you enjoy sports without your body? Remember
that healthy bodies come in many sizes and shapes, including fat but fit.
Declaration of Independence
From a Weight-Obsessed World
| declare, from this day forward, | will choose to live my life by the
following tenets. In doing so, | declare myself free and independent
from the pressures and constraints of a weight-obsessed world.
* | will accept my body in its natural size and shape.
| will celebrate all that my body can do for me each day.
* Iwill treat my body with respect, give it enough rest, fuel it with a
variety of foods, exercise it moderately, and listen to what it needs.
| will choose to resist our society’s pressures to judge myself and
other people on physical characteristics like body weight, shape,
or size. | will respect people based on their depth of character
and the impact of their accomplishments.
* | will refuse to deny my body valuable nutrients by dieting or
using weight-loss products.
| will avoid categorizing foods as either “good” or “bad.” | will
not associate guilt or shame with eating certain foods. Instead,
| will nourish my body with a balance of foods, listening and
responding to what it needs.
* | will not use food to mask my emotional needs.
| will not avoid participating in activities that | enjoy (e.g., swim-
ming, dancing, eating a meal) simply because | am self-conscious
about the way my body looks. | will recognize that | have the
right to enjoy any activity regardless of my body shape or size.
| will believe that my self-esteem and identity come from within!
Courtesy of the National Eating Disorders Association, www.nationaleatingdisorders.org.
